A score is a claim about the future: roughly how well a model will predict data it has
not seen. This section makes that claim honest in three steps, on the same simulated
survey as the rest of the course. Cross-validation, with folds of sites, map blocks or
years, scores a model on data far enough from its training data; the measure is chosen
to suit the use of the predictions; and resampling the sites puts an interval on the
score, so two models can be compared fairly.

{{< video https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yVOEkCqrOec title="Validation: when to believe a score" >}}

## Further resources

**Documentation**

- [Evaluate your model with resampling](https://www.tidymodels.org/start/resampling/), tidymodels.
- [rsample](https://rsample.tidymodels.org/) and [yardstick](https://yardstick.tidymodels.org/), tidymodels. Every resampling scheme, and every metric with its definition.
- [Cross-validation](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/cross_validation.html) and [metrics and scoring](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/model_evaluation.html), scikit-learn user guide. Its section on grouped data covers cross-validation by site.
